key_insight: ThinkJEPA couples a latent world model with a large vision–language reasoning model so that latent forecasts are grounded in high-level semantics, enabling more accurate long-horizon prediction beyond short observation windows.
problem_solved: Latent world models trained on dense short-horizon prediction tend to extrapolate low-level, local dynamics and miss long-term semantic structure; the paper addresses lack of semantic grounding and limited temporal context in video forecasting.
method: Augment a latent world model (e.g., V-JEPA2 style predictor) with a large vision–language reasoning model that operates over latent representations to provide semantic context and high-level reasoning.
Align and distill VLM outputs into the latent predictor as conditioning/regularization so future latent states reflect language-grounded semantics rather than only low-level extrapolation.
Use the combined model for hierarchical, longer-horizon forecasting (latent autoregression + semantic prompts) to improve downstream tasks such as planning, retrieval, and captioning.
impact: Provides a practical way to inject rich semantic knowledge into compact latent world models, improving long-horizon prediction fidelity and downstream utility for tasks that require semantic understanding (e.g., planning, video understanding) without relying solely on dense pixel supervision.

paper_title: ThinkJEPA: Empowering Latent World Models with Large Vision-Language Reasoning Model
paper_authors: Haichao Zhang, Yijiang Li, Shwai He, Tushar Nagarajan, Mingfei Chen
